facts.statement: The study is a retrospective analysis of patients with AL amyloid neuropathy seen at a university hospital in Paris, France.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In 77% of the patients, peripheral neuropathy was the first sign of the disease, and 43% had no other organ involvement at diagnosis, a condition the authors call pure neuropathic AL amyloidosis.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Among patients with pure neuropathic AL amyloidosis, 80% had a chronic, length-dependent axonal polyneuropathy, a pattern that is often nonspecific.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The IgM subtype of AL amyloidosis made up 29% of the cases and was particularly associated with pure neuropathic AL amyloidosis.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In 20% of the patients, abnormalities in serum free light chains were the only hematological clue to the diagnosis.
facts.subject: humans
